turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm reviewing the new evaluation suite for our agent framework. I want to tweak how we score the models.
Sure. Are you looking at latency, accuracy, or something else?

Mostly efficiency. I've been reading Sarah Sachs' recent blog post. She argues we should stop looking at single-step accuracy and start evaluating AI performance based on cost per capability per second over whole tool-use trajectories.
That’s a strong metric for real-world deployment. It penalizes agents that take many cheap but slow steps just to get the right answer.
Exactly. It forces the model to be efficient, not just correct. I need to draft a memo to the engineering team proposing this shift in our benchmarking strategy.
Got it. I can help draft that. Should I emphasize the business impact of the cost savings?
Yes. Also, can you check if the coffee machine is back online? It was making a weird grinding noise earlier.
I don't have access to the office IoT sensors, so I can't check the machine status. I recommend asking facilities.
Right. Back to the memo: please outline the key argument for adopting Sarah's metric over our current pass@1 score.
I will draft an outline focusing on why trajectory-level efficiency matters more than isolated step correctness for our use case.
